$comment: Accepted CodeQL findings for the javascript-typescript language, with the disposition that GitHub code scanning carries as a dismissal. Each entry: { rule, path, count, reason, expires }. scripts/security/check-codeql-sarif.mjs fails the build when a CodeQL SARIF contains a warning/error result that is NOT covered here, when the count for a listed (rule, path) is exceeded, or when an entry is missing a reason or has expired (fail-closed, the same contract as config/security/pqc-allowlist.json and config/security/lockfile-freshness-allowlist.json). CodeQL for JavaScript does NOT honour inline `// codeql[...]` suppression comments, so this file - not an in-code annotation - is the operative mechanism. NOTE-level results are ignored: they are quality queries, and the largest such class (unused local variables) is gated by the `no-unused-vars` ESLint rule instead.

acceptedFindings.reason: Intentional: dev verification script uploads repo-controlled authorization-model.json to a local OpenFGA server (default 127.0.0.1:8080). File-to-HTTP taint is the purpose; no untrusted input.

Intentional: local i18n script translates missing pack strings via Google and writes validated results (placeholder protection + native-script checks) into marketMessagePacks. Dev-only tool; never shipped.
FP: sink is writeJsonAtomic; content is JSON-escaped and the path is hard-allowlisted to repo root/tmpdir before write. Rationale: docs/security/code-scanning-triage-2026-09-14.md
False positive: trusted-host and private-network SSRF checks run before a hashed file is written into a private cache. Tests cover localhost, metadata IPs, private DNS, and untrusted hosts.

False positive: the release id passes a strict charset validator (alphanumerics plus . _ + @ / only) before reaching cmd.exe argv, so no injection is possible. The codeql[] suppression comment is present on the flagged line but not honored by this analysis.
This is an HMAC-SHA256 signature for LiveKit access tokens, not a password hash. A fast keyed MAC is the correct primitive for token signing; bcrypt or another password KDF would be incorrect here.
False positive: test fixture derives the same HIBP k-anonymity lookup token for a mocked range response - never password storage. Inline codeql[] suppression present but not honored by this analysis.

False positive: the SHA-1 is the k-anonymity lookup token for the HIBP range API (fixed protocol requirement), never used to store or verify a password. Inline codeql[] suppression comments are present on the flagged line but are not honored by this analysis.
